title: finding.v1
description: One finding from a pack's run. The source of truth is findings.json in .agency/runs/<run-id>/; anything derived from it can be thrown away and rebuilt at any time.

id.description: ULID. Never autoincrement — otherwise merging two histories collides.

pack.description: Name of the pack that produced this finding — a skill in .claude/skills/agency-<name>/.

dimension.description: Which of the pack's dimensions found this. Lets precision be measured per dimension.

type.description: What kind of output this is — `finding` when absent, which is every output written before types existed. The pack declares how each of its types is handled (`pack.json` → `outputs`): whether it deduplicates, what evidence it needs, what feedback it accepts, whether it may act, whether it may become memory. The core reads that policy and never the meaning: it does not know what a `bet` or a `decision` is, and the moment it does, every future specialist has to pretend to be a code reviewer again.

body.description: Markdown. The claim plus a concrete failure scenario (inputs/state → wrong output).

anchor.description: A four-layer anchor. Resolved top to bottom, stopping at the first layer that succeeds. Without it a finding points at innocent code after a few weeks and has no way to know it.

file.description: POSIX path relative to the project root. Never absolute — otherwise the run record could not be shared or committed.

commit.description: The full 40 characters. A shortened SHA can later point somewhere else without warning.

snippet.description: Layer 2. The text of the line..endLine block on the day of the analysis. The most distinctive line in it is what gets searched for — a one-line snippet fails on '/**' and similar boilerplate.

symbol.description: Layer 3, from the symbol in the graph. Survives a refactor and a moved block where a line number does not.

body.description: Layer 4. The symbol's body on the day of the analysis. A safety net for when the commit no longer exists in the clone — a squash-merge with the branch deleted is GitHub's default.

evidence.description: The deterministic gate: a finding with no evidence never becomes a candidate. This is not a text-quality filter, it is a schema — such a finding simply does not validate.

kind.description: Two generations. WITHOUT a locator (older, still valid): graph = a fact from the code-graph driver (`agency graph`), rule = a rule from the project's own documentation, test-gap = missing coverage, diff = content of the change, runtime = observed behaviour, doc = contradicts the documentation. WITH a locator (since 2026-09-06, machine-verifiable): code = a place in the source at a commit, document = a file in the repository at a commit, command = something that ran in this run, web_snapshot = a page fetched in this run and kept, board_item = an item in a board snapshot taken by this run.

source.description: Where this came from — e.g. 'agency graph impact --depth 2' or 'CLAUDE.md#rules-that-will-bite-you'. Free text, and that is the point of `locator`: a source can be written without ever having been opened. Kept because committed run history is full of it, and because a pointer to a document that needs no verification is honest.

locator.description: Where the proof is, in a shape a machine can open — the half `source` never had. Verified against what THIS RUN recorded and never against the live world: the gate is offline, or `agency replay` stops meaning anything and the same run stops giving the same answer.

file.description: POSIX path relative to the project root, as in `anchor.file`.

command.description: The command line, as it was run. Flags are not compared — only the command and its subcommands.

artifact.description: What the run kept, as a path inside its own RUN_DIR. Always under `evidence/`, never absolute and never out of the run: an artifact somewhere else is one the run cannot vouch for.

ref.description: Identity of the thing inside the artifact — an issue number, a board item id.

score.description: Confidence after the false-positive filter. Below the project's threshold a finding is not published, but it stays in the run record. Required since 2026-09-06: while it was optional the threshold could be walked around by saying nothing, and the one number that shows a miscalibrated pack — the score distribution against precision — had a bucket full of unknowns. Findings written before that are left alone; they are an older population, and `agency validate --fix` does not invent a number for them.

scoreReason.description: One sentence: what would have to be different for this score to be lower. Not a summary of the finding — a statement of what the confidence rests on, which is the part that can turn out to be wrong.

fingerprint.description: Deterministic fingerprint for dedup across runs. Computed from the symbol and the normalized claim, NOT from the line number or the title — a title survives a corrected diagnosis, the content does not.

state.description: Five states. `candidate` rests only where the pack has no sink; `held` waits for the next chain member; `sent` and `rejected` are terminal; a decision event in decisions.jsonl carries who and why.

sinks.description: Where the finding propagated to. Derived destinations, not the source of truth — when a sink fails, the finding is not lost.
